recommendation: Keep this audit commit as-is. Future Questionnaire changes should preserve the answerConstraint-based representation of open-choice behavior rather than reintroducing open-choice into Questionnaire.item.type.
issue_request: FHIR-14097 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Questionnaire correction for STU3 asking that invariant que-10 allow maxLength on open-choice items because open-choice permits a string answer.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 13242, represented by git commit a0608f74fe11d33b9ce176ed7c6e52e1190c20ae, which added open-choice to the old Questionnaire spreadsheet que-10 expression. The follow-up Questionnaire task commit 651aa532afe40d621b6a593df3fabc0b86b0af62 mentioned GF#14097 but did not establish a different rule.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in source/fhir.ini. Later Published issue FHIR-20396 removed choice/open-choice from Questionnaire.item.type and added Questionnaire.item.answerConstraint; the active code system defines optionsOrString as permitting free-text string answers. FHIR-49226 later edited the same que-10 invariant for date/dateTime/time maxLength support without changing the open-choice successor semantics.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml has que-10 allowing maxLength for simple item types or answerConstraint='optionsOrString', and source/questionnaire/codesystem-questionnaire-answer-constraint.xml defines optionsOrString.

related_jiras.note: Removed choice/open-choice from Questionnaire.item.type and moved the open-choice behavior into answerConstraint, explaining the current representation of the FHIR-14097 rule. Already represented on the combined branch.
